packet.headline_seed: Ethiopian woman's joy at rare quintuplets after 12 years trying for a baby
packet.description_seed: The woman, 35, says she was praying for a baby and was "overjoyed" to be "blessed with five at once".

what: Ethiopian woman's joy at rare quintuplets after 12 years trying for a baby

clean_source_blocks.text: A woman has given birth to rare quintuplets in Ethiopia's Harari Regional state after 12 years of trying for a baby. Bedriya Adem said she and her husband were "overjoyed" to be "blessed with five children at once". The 35-year-old delivered four boys and a girl, all of whom are in "full health", at the Hiwot Fana Specialised Hospital, the hospital said. "I cannot express my happiness in words," she told the BBC, recalling how she was "filled with depression and pain" until her prayers were answered. Hospital medical director Dr Mohammed Nur Abdulahi said the mother and babies remained under medical care at the hospital. The babies weighed between 1.3 and 1.4kg (3lb). He told the BBC that newborns who weigh more than a kilogram have a high chance of survival and healthy growth.
The woman, 35, says she was praying for a baby and was "overjoyed" to be "blessed with five at once".

"I prayed for just one child, and Allah gave me five," she said, talking about how she felt during her "long wait". The first-time mother said her husband already had a child from another marriage, who lived with them. "He used to tell me that having [the other child] was enough and that I should not worry, but deep inside I was suffering - psychologically and emotionally - as the entire village questioned my inability to giver birth," she said. "What I endured in the past feels like a distant dream, one I do not even want to recall," she added. "I spent 12 years in pain, hiding myself, and praying constantly for children - at last, Allah heard me."

The doctor told the BBC that Bedriya had conceived naturally, without the aid of in vitro fertilisation (IVF), which the hospital does not offer. IVF can increase the chance of multiple births if more than one embryo can be transferred. The chance of conceiving quintuplets naturally is about one in 55 million. The doctor said the birth had been through Caesarean on Tuesday evening. "She received regular medical care during her pregnancy and was informed that she had conceived more than one baby. She had full and proper medical assistance throughout," Mohammed said, as he described her "excitement". Bedriya said she had initially been told she was pregnant with four babies, but when she gave birth, there was one more.

[Lähde: BBC World]
A woman has given birth to rare quintuplets in Ethiopia's Harari Regional state after 12 years of trying for a baby.

Bedriya Adem said she and her husband were "overjoyed" to be "blessed with five children at once".

The 35-year-old delivered four boys and a girl, all of whom are in "full health", at the Hiwot Fana Specialised Hospital, the hospital said.

"I cannot express my happiness in words," she told the BBC, recalling how she was "filled with depression and pain" until her prayers were answered.

Hospital medical director Dr Mohammed Nur Abdulahi said the mother and babies remained under medical care at the hospital. The babies weighed between 1.3 and 1.4kg (3lb).

He told the BBC that newborns who weigh more than a kilogram have a high chance of survival and healthy growth.

The doctor told the BBC that Bedriya had conceived naturally, without the aid of in vitro fertilisation (IVF), which the hospital does not offer.

IVF can increase the chance of multiple births if more than one embryo can be transferred.

The chance of conceiving quintuplets naturally is about one in 55 million.

The doctor said the birth had been through Caesarean on Tuesday evening.

"She received regular medical care during her pregnancy and was informed that she had conceived more than one baby. She had full and proper medical assistance throughout," Mohammed said, as he described her "excitement".

Bedriya said she had initially been told she was pregnant with four babies, but when she gave birth, there was one more.

"I prayed for just one child, and Allah gave me five," she said, talking about how she felt during her "long wait".

The first-time mother said her husband already had a child from another marriage, who lived with them.

"He used to tell me that having [the other child] was enough and that I should not worry, but deep inside I was suffering - psychologically and emotionally - as the entire village questioned my inability to giver birth," she said.

"What I endured in the past feels like a distant dream, one I do not even want to recall," she added.

"I spent 12 years in pain, hiding myself, and praying constantly for children - at last, Allah heard me."

She said that she was a subsistence farmer and was not sure how she would provide for her newly enlarged family. "But I believe Allah will provide, through the support of my community and the government."

Their "five blessings" have been named Naif, Ammar, Munzir, Nazira, and Ansar.

payload.title: Etiopialaisnainen sai harvinaiset viitoset 12 vuoden odotuksen jälkeen
payload.summary: Etiopiassa 35-vuotias Bedriya Adem on synnyttänyt viitoset vuosien lapsitoiveen jälkeen. Neljä poikaa ja yksi tyttö syntyivät keisarileikkauksella Hararin osavaltiossa, ja sairaalan mukaan sekä äiti että lapset ovat hoidossa.
payload.content:
Etiopiassa 35-vuotias Bedriya Adem on synnyttänyt harvinaiset viitoset 12 vuoden lapsitoiveen jälkeen. Hararin osavaltiossa sijaitsevan Hiwot Fana -erikoissairaalan mukaan lapset, neljä poikaa ja yksi tyttö, ovat täydessä terveydessä, mutta sekä äiti että vastasyntyneet ovat edelleen sairaalahoidossa.

## Pitkä odotus päättyi yllätykseen

Adem kertoi kokeneensa pitkän odotuksen aikana masennusta ja kipua. Hänen mukaansa kyläyhteisön kyselyt lapsettomuudesta lisäsivät henkistä painetta. Hän kuvasi perheen iloa suureksi, kun vuosien rukoukset päättyivät viiden lapsen syntymään.

Adem on ensisynnyttäjä. Hänen miehellään oli ennestään lapsi toisesta avioliitosta, ja perheessä oli hänen mukaansa yritetty lohduttaa häntä sillä, että kotona oli jo lapsi. Adem kertoi kuitenkin kärsineensä asiasta syvästi ja rukoilleensa jatkuvasti lapsia.

Sairaalan mukaan Ademille oli raskauden aikana kerrottu, että hän odotti useampaa kuin yhtä lasta. Hänelle oli aluksi sanottu, että lapsia olisi neljä, mutta synnytyksessä heitä olikin viisi.

## Lääkäri: raskaus alkoi luonnollisesti

Sairaalan lääketieteellinen johtaja Mohammed Nur Abdulahi kertoi, että raskaus oli alkanut luonnollisesti ilman koeputkihedelmöitystä. Sairaalan mukaan se ei tarjoa koeputkihedelmöityshoitoja. Monikkoraskauksien todennäköisyys voi kasvaa hedelmöityshoidoissa, jos kohtuun siirretään useampi alkio.

Luonnollisesti alkaneiden viitosraskauksien kerrotaan olevan erittäin harvinaisia: mahdollisuudeksi on arvioitu noin yksi 55 miljoonasta. Lapset syntyivät keisarileikkauksella tiistai-iltana.

## Vastasyntyneet jäivät seurantaan

Vastasyntyneet painoivat 1,3–1,4 kiloa. Abdulahin mukaan yli kilon painoisilla vastasyntyneillä on hyvät mahdollisuudet selviytyä ja kasvaa terveesti, mutta äiti ja lapset tarvitsevat edelleen sairaalan hoitoa ja seurantaa.

Abdulahin mukaan Adem sai raskauden aikana säännöllistä hoitoa ja asianmukaista lääketieteellistä tukea. Hänelle oli myös kerrottu jo raskauden aikana, että kyseessä oli monikkoraskaus. Adem kuvasi syntymää suuren ilon hetkeksi pitkän odotuksen jälkeen.

Sairaalan mukaan äiti ja lapset ovat hoidossa, ja vastasyntyneet ovat täydessä terveydessä.
Lääkärin mukaan raskaus alkoi luonnollisesti ilman koeputkihedelmöitystä.
